name: Hereditary Neuropathy with Liability to Pressure Palsies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for HNPP

criteria.description: Recurrent, transient focal neuropathies precipitated by minor trauma or compression
Electrophysiological evidence of demyelinating neuropathy with conduction block at common entrapment sites
Identification of PMP22 gene deletion or mutation
Positive family history of similar neuropathic episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent pressure palsies plus electrophysiological evidence and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; electrophysiological studies are essential for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent focal mononeuropathies triggered by minor compression
searchTerms: repeated nerve damage from minor pressure
focal nerve palsies triggered by compression

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient sensory loss or paresthesia in affected nerve distribution
searchTerms: brief sensory loss in nerve area

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness in distribution of compressed nerves
searchTerms: muscle weakness in compressed nerve area
localized muscle weakness from nerve damage

common.symptomName: Hypoesthesia or numbness in peripheral nerve territories
searchTerms: loss of feeling in nerve territories

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to peroneal nerve palsy
Painless nerve enlargement (tomacula) on nerve biopsy
common.notes: Usually detected histologically rather than clinically

occasional.symptomName: Paresthesia in hands or feet unrelated to compression events
Pain or discomfort at sites of nerve compression

searchTerms: problems with facial and head nerves
nerve issues affecting face and head

laboratory: Nerve conduction studies showing focal slowing and conduction block at common entrapment sites
Nerve biopsy demonstrating tomacula (focal myelin thickenings)
imaging: MRI neurography may show nerve enlargement at compression sites
genetic: Deletion of PMP22 gene on chromosome 17p11.2
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy without recurrent focal palsies
Diffuse demyelinating neuropathy rather than focal conduction block
PMP22 gene duplication rather than deletion

redFlags: Persistent or progressive weakness without recovery
Systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats
references: Lupski JR et al. Hereditary Neuropathy with Liability to Pressure Palsies. GeneReviews, 2020.
Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
Bird TD. Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies. In: Adam MP, et al., editors. GeneReviews, 2019.
